proposition: Let a_0 = 5, a_1 = 24 and a_n = 9*a_(n-1) + (-18)*a_(n-2) for n >= 2. Then for every n with 0 <= n <= 30, a_n = 2*3^n + 3*6^n.
hypotheses: the recurrence is applied only for n >= 2

argument.text: At n = 0 the closed form gives 5, matching a_0 = 5.
At n = 1 the closed form gives 24, matching a_1 = 24.
The closed form satisfies the recurrence: for every n in [0, 28], f(n+2) = 9*f(n+1) + (-18)*f(n).
Put H(n) = n^2 + [n = 3]. Then (n-3)n^2 = (n-3)H(n) for every n in [1, 30].
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30, n^3 is congruent to n modulo 6.
For every integer n with 2 <= n <= 30 we have n^2 >= 2n.
For every integer n with 1 <= n <= 30: if n is divisible by 4 then n(n+1)/2 is even.
The identity n^3 - n = 120 is verified directly at n = 5.
Every integer n in [1, 30] satisfies n^2 > 30.
Two base cases plus the recurrence identity give the closed form for every n in [0, 30].
